title: Chain of responsibility: handle it or pass it on
summary: Approvers are linked by spending limit. Each approves what it can and forwards the rest unchanged; the caller knows only the first link, and the end of the chain rejects.
code: # Each approver handles what it can and forwards the rest; callers only know the first.
triggers: the first of several handlers able to deal with a request should take it, tried in order, without the sender choosing
escalation levels, middleware and fallbacks: approvals by amount, support tiers, cash dispensers
prompts: Support tickets go to a chatbot first; whatever it can't answer goes to a first-line agent, then to an engineer. Customers only submit the ticket and never pick the level.
A loan request is reviewed by an automatic scorer, then a branch officer, then a credit committee, and the first one allowed to decide on that amount does.
invariant: Each approver either answers or forwards the unchanged request to its successor; exactly one link answers, or the end of the chain rejects.
mantra: Handle it or hand it on.
pitfalls: Forward by calling the successor's approve(), so the request keeps travelling.
Decide what the end of the chain does: reject, return a default or raise.
Unlike a decorator, a handler that answers stops the chain; unlike an observer, only one handler acts.

anchors.name: ATM cash withdrawal
anchors.trick: Each note dispenser pays what it can and passes the remainder down.

anchors.name: Expense approval workflow
anchors.trick: Manager, director and CFO links, each with a spending limit.

mutations.explanation: Names the next approver without asking it, so every amount above the manager's limit lands on the director, even 1,000,000.
Off by one at the limit: a manager may approve exactly 1,000, but this escalates it.
